Good morning, everyone, Excellencies, distinguished speakers, ladies and gentlemen. On behalf of the Committee on the Exercise of the Inalienable Rights of the Palestinian People, it is my privilege to welcome you to today's briefing on Human Dignity Under Strain: The Humanitarian and Human Rights Consequences in the Occupied Palestinian Territory. For those watching us on UN Web TV from around the world, my name is Nazira binti Osman. I am the Vice Chair of the UN Palestinian Rights Committee and the Permanent Representative of Malaysia to the United Nations in New York. On behalf of the Committee, let me express our appreciation to all of you for joining us today. We are pleased to have with us today Ms. Francesca Albanese. United Nations Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights in the Palestinian territories occupied since 1967, Ms. Farida Shahid, United Nations Special Rapporteur on the right to education, Mr. Surya Deva, United Nations Special Rapporteur on the right to development, as well as Mr. Srinivasan Muralidhar, Chair of the Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory. I thank our distinguished briefers for joining us today, and I look forward to a frank and meaningful discussion. So we will begin with briefings by our speakers, to be followed by a Q&A session, and then concluding remarks by Minister Riad Mansour, the Permanent Observer of the State of Palestine to the United Nations in New York. Let us now start with our first briefer, UN Special Rapporteur Ms. Francesca Albanese. So since May 2022, Ms. Albanese has served as the United Nations Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights in the Palestinian territories since 1967. In her recent reports to the Human Rights Council, Special Rapporteur Albanese examined allegations of systematic torture and ill-treatment of Palestinians since October 2023 and placed them within the broader context of grave violations of international law. The most recent report argues that the suppression of Palestinian journalists, Israeli propaganda and censorship, and international media bias have enabled atrocities and obstructed accountability through a process termed “mediacity”. She has also drawn attention to the impact of expanding movement restrictions in the occupied West Bank, restrictions that affect access to healthcare, education, employment, and family life. It is unfortunate that Ms. Albanese is unable to be here with us in person due to unjust sanctions imposed on her. Nevertheless, we are grateful that she is able to join us online today. Ms. Albanese, you have the floor.
Ms. Vice Chair, Excellencies, colleagues and friends, thank you, Ambassador Osman, and thank you.
To the committee for convening this briefing.
I also like to salute Ambassador Mansoor. I'm glad to be joined by my fellow mandate holders and by the chair of the Commission of Inquiry.
I regret that I can only address you remotely, indeed, that the UN-appointed expert cannot enter the city where the United Nations sits because of sanctions against her for doing Her job says something about the state of the United Nations, our system, and multilateralism. Earlier this week, I presented my report, my ninth report, to the Third Committee. It's titled "Truth Under the Rubble: Media in the Time of Genocide." The report shows that the destruction of truth has become part of the destruction of a people. the destruction of a people that I have documented for more than three years and that we should have seen coming, as the Palestinians themselves did. But we didn't believe them, or perhaps we lacked the courage to believe what they've been telling us through and through. Since October 2023, Israel has killed nearly 300 journalists and media workers in Gaza. Among them are camera operators struck in double tap attacks, and reporters labeled terrorists after their deaths or undisclosed or discredited evidence. Hundreds of their relatives have been killed as well. Media offices and most of Gaza's telecommunication infrastructure have been destroyed, and foreign journalists have been barred from the territory for three years. Inside Israel, segments of the media have normalized the dehumanization and at times explicitly called for Gaza's annihilation. These calls continue despite a binding order of the International Court of Justice to prevent and punish incitement to genocide. Abroad, influential outlets and digital platforms have too often reproduced the perpetrator's narrative. They've censored Palestinian voices, and in some cases, they've taken money to deny even a famine.
Called in my last report, media side. When witnesses are eliminated and evidence is erased, the crime is not only committed, it is concealed, and impunity becomes part of the plan. But this is part and parcel of a bigger genocidal scheme. Since October 2023, more than 74,500 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza, and over 175,000 injured, according to the latest available figures. More than 21,000 of these were children.
More than 58,000 children have lost one or both parents, and.
Thousands of them have survived only to face a lifetime altered by injury. Gaza has the highest number of child amputees per capita in the world. More than 5,000 amputations have been recorded, around one in five involving a child, many carried out without anesthesia. Many of the tens of thousands of survivors face permanent disabilities, while the destruction of health care and rehabilitation services denies them the care, prosthetics, and support they urgently need. I wish I could tell you the so-called ceasefire had brought relief. It does not. Since it was announced a year ago, more than 1,500 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza. And Israeli attacks have continued on an almost everyday basis. This past week alone, children were killed, a university campus was struck twice, and tent camps were set ablaze. Bakeries are now closed because flour is blocked. Hospital generators are running out of fuel again. Families shelter in rainwater pits and buildings on the verge of collapse as winter approaches again. In the West Bank, the pattern of erasure is also accelerating, because after the attack at Tiberia checkpoints on 23 October, the Prime Minister of Israel, ICC, wanted to destroy the attackers' neighborhood, to change it completely, and to evacuate its residents. Within days, thousands of Palestinians were forcibly displaced from Hebron and hundreds of homes were raided. Dozens of people were detained. The entire communities in Masafra and Yatta were sealed off, and the whole territory has been locked down. This is collective punishment. prohibited by the Fourth Geneva Convention, unfolding alongside a record olive harvest season of settler violence, more than 270 attacks in less than two months, often in the presence of soldiers. All these while land is declared state land and new settlement tenders are issued. But What I find infuriating of all these excellencies, that what we are witnessing has a name, and those who name it are no longer isolated voices. In January 2024, the International Court of Justice found the right of the Palestinians in Gaza to be protected from genocide plausible and at the real and imminent risk, and ordered Israel to prevent genocidal act. In July 2024, the court found Israel's continued presence in the occupied Palestinian territory totally unlawful and to be ended as rapidly as possible and unconditionally. It also found a breach of the prohibition of racial segregation and apartheid. Israeli historians and Holocaust scholars, among whom Razi Gal, Amos Goldberg, Omar Bartov, reached the conclusion of genocide, and so did Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch, the International Association of Genocide Scholars, Israeli organizations, B'Tselem, Physicians for Human Rights. And in September 2025, the independent International Commission of Inquiry, whose chair is with us today, concluded that genocide is being committed in Gaza. So the fact had been established, and the law has been applied under the Genocide Convention. every state's duty to prevent arose once a serious risk of genocide became known. After the court's order of January 2024, no state could claim ignorance. And so, the international community has yet to mobilize in proportion to these findings. Rather, the contrary is true, in fact.
Trade continues, especially of the oil and gas which is fueling occupation, apartheid, colonization, and genocide. And so do investment, diplomatic cover, and the welcoming of individuals subject to arrest warrants of the International Criminal Court, to the very same place where I, a UN Special Rapporteur, am prohibited to enter. The state able to make a difference have offered statements instead of measures, and recognition of Palestine without action to end the occupation that makes a Palestinian state impossible. Mr. Chair, this brings me to my central message. I fear that many in the UN underestimate what is at stake. Nowhere is the failure clearer than in the abandonment of Angua. The agency that is the lifeline of millions of Palestine refugees and the backbone of humanitarian response in Gaza, it has been legislated against by Israel, its premises attacked, and hundreds of its staff killed. It has been defamed through the allegations of systemic infiltration that were amplified by media and never substantiated. Several donors suspended funding on that basis and plunged the agency into crisis. The International Court of Justice itself has since confirmed apartheid Israel's obligation to facilitate the work of UNRWA. And still, the defense of a UN body by its own member states has been timid at best. The United Nations was built on the ashes of two world wars and one of the worst genocides in human history. The Genocide Convention was adopted the day before the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. The convention was promised that the world would never again stand by while a people was destroyed, the declaration that every human being's dignity would be protected. If these promises fail here in the most documented genocide in history, under the eyes of the court, the commission, the treaty body, special procedures, the damage will not stay in Palestine. Every perpetrator everywhere will draw the lesson that the law is optional and that its institution can be starved, smeared, and sanctioned into silence. Institutions rarely collapse in a single moment. They hollow out, failure after unanswered failure, until no one believes them anymore. Gaza might be the breaking point, not because the United Nations lacks the tools, but because its members chose not to use them. It is not too late.
Implement the court's orders and the General Assembly's resolution, suspend arms transfer and trade that sustain unlawful.
Occupation and genocide, fund and protect UNRWA, protect the journalists, preserve the record, because accountability depends on it. Do not forget the people of Palestine. History will ask what each of us did. Let our answer not be that we just watched.
Ms. Albaneese, I thank you for your important and very frank briefing on the situation in the occupied Palestinian territory. Your work continues to shed light. on the realities on the ground and contributes meaningfully to the international efforts aimed at upholding international law and ensuring respect for the rights and dignity of the Palestinian people. The Committee greatly appreciates your unwavering commitment, professionalism, tireless efforts in the pursuit of justice, accountability, and the protection of human rights. I will now give the floor to our next briefer, Ms. Farida Shahid, who has been the UN Special Rapporteur on the right to education since August 2022. Special Rapporteur Shahid has emphasized that the right to education is not merely about access to a classroom. It requires an educational environment in which children can learn, develop, and participate meaningfully. Her recent work reminds us how fragile that right becomes when schools, teachers, and students are placed under sustained pressure. Ms. Shahid, the floor is yours.
Thank you. Madam Chair, Excellencies, colleagues, and friends, I thank you for this opportunity. Education is an inalienable human right, regardless of the circumstances, location, and identity of the learners. Today, the scale of destruction, the displacement, school closures, restrictions on movement mean that the Palestinian youth and children stand dispossessed of this fundamental right to learn, to think, to express their opinion freely. The right to education, which is a gateway to so many other rights, is protected under both international human rights law and international humanitarian law, and it remains fully applicable during armed conflict. Schools as civilian objects, students and staff as civilians are expressly protected, and Israel has obligations under international law to ensure the right in the occupied Palestinian territory. Instead, what we have seen and we continue to witness is scholasticide, the systemic and systematic obliteration of education, which has been horrendous in Gaza. 98% of the schools and all 13 universities have been destroyed. The arrest, detention, and killings of teachers, students, and staff is appalling. Almost 21,000 Palestinian students have been killed. a classroom of children every day during the war on Gaza. At least 173 have been killed in the West Bank. Almost 170,000 have been injured. More than a thousand teachers, lecturers, administrative staff members have been killed across the territories. Of the 394 UNRWA staff who have been killed in Gaza, 259, that's the vast majority, were either providing or supporting education. And it hasn't ended, as we just heard from the Special Rapporteur Francesco. Since the so-called ceasefire, one child has been killed at least every day. Hundreds have been wounded. Virtually all under five children in Gaza are malnourished. Nearly one in three go without food for more than 24 hours or more, and food deprivation amongst young children leads to wasting and stunting, which in turn causes irreparable physical and cognitive impairments, impacting an entire generation of students in their learning. We now have the World Food Program warning us that with its reduced funds, there will be half a million more people will not be provided with food in Palestine. The UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry investigating attacks on education, facilities, religious and cultural sites has also concluded that the Israeli attacks amount to war crimes and the crime against humanity of extermination. Scholasticide is multigenerational. It aims to dismantle the very foundation of Palestinian society, erase their history, and destroy a sense of collective self. This is why, apart from all the schools and universities that were attacked and destroyed, 13 libraries, and the central archives of Gaza with 150 years of history, 195 heritage sites, 227 mosques, three churches at least, were destroyed or targeted. For when education is destroyed, so too are the hopes and dreams of the people. Education's not just about accumulating skills, and certainly not about market skills. It's a means of developing critical thinking and a sense of who you are. And in conflict, it is a lifeline, and it provides children and youth with a sense of normalcy when everything else is chaotic and a trauma. Over 830,000 children in the West Bank and East Jerusalem have returned to school amidst security threats. Students have told me, we live in fear from one day to the next at all times of the day. Fears of arrest, beatings, and imprisonment. And I've written on this report on safety and education and also a report on education conflict situations. You cannot learn if you do not feel safe and are not safe in the teaching environment. Last September, 10 out of 48 schools were demolished in East Jerusalem. Some schools were closed or some had to close as they failed to get licenses, which are often conditional on curriculum correction, which really means deleting references to Palestinian history and culture. Students studying the Palestinian curricula say, "We're scared to take our schoolbooks with us." Because children and their fathers are fined for having Palestinian books, especially post 2023. And unique to Jerusalem is students under house arrest. In the West Bank, the presence of military near schools and at checkpoints often leads to intimidation of those who are trying to access schools and denial of access. This heightens distress and insecurity, and stops students and teachers and staff from reaching schools. In the first half of the year, there were 224 security incidents, which affected 152 schools, 20,450 students, and at least 859 educational personnel.
21% of all the security breaches were due to settler violence, which we see continues to spiral out of control and has the complicity of the Israeli security forces who are seen on television and elsewhere standing by or helping. Settler violence has also displaced at least 1,700 children from school. Military incursions into the West Bank educational facilities, including UNRWA schools, disrupts learning and exposes children as young as six to violence, tear gas, injury, and lasting trauma. Continued military operations prevent students from Jenin and Nour Shams camps in the north, then West Bank, returning to regular schools. The psychological and physical damage is overwhelming. As you just heard, Gaza is home to the highest number of per capita child amputees in the world. The trauma of bombs, bereavement, violence, and fear will plague children throughout their lives. In Gaza, the trauma includes amputations without anesthesia, as one Palestinian father saying, "Seeing things children should never see, dismembered limbs and decomposing bodies." Students tell me, "Our childhood has been stolen." On turning 15, a girl said that she felt she turned 40 because she had to look after the injured, find water and food for herself and the family to survive. So I'm always deeply touched by pictures that I still continue to see of children scrambling over rubble, determined to get to school despite all the challenges. Students from Gaza wanting to study abroad have also faced hugely complex It's restrictive multi-layered processes for exit permits, which are controlled by the Israeli military. Many with international admissions and scholarships cannot proceed abroad. Visas, too, are an issue, as we saw in October. 55 scholars admitted in Irish universities were denied visa. Very few have managed to actually proceed abroad. And the role of UNRWA is absolutely critical. It reaches over 100,000 children in temporary learning spaces, 275 remotely, thousands, sorry, 275,000 remotely. More than 1.1 million children in Gaza need mental health and psychosocial support, and UNRWA has provided this for half a million. And it's supporting some 10,000 unaccompanied, separated, and vulnerable children, including 3,000 plus children with disabilities. But the drone strikes and gunfire in or near learning spaces is taking place in the learning spaces, in tents and windowless buildings have injured children and parents, increased insecurity, leading to more and more parents withdrawing their children. The international community has an absolute responsibility to end the school hostage site, restore childhoods, and ensure the right to education in the OPT, securing a lasting end to hostilities is vital and a precondition for so much else. The longer children are out of school, the more difficult it is to catch up, and the higher the risk of child labor, early marriages, and recruitment by armed groups. Special Rapporteurs have repeatedly pointed out the numerous ways in which Israel is violating both international humanitarian law and international human rights law, and states should consider measures to ensure that Israel complies with its obligations under these laws. The right to education must be protected as a lifeline, rebuilding must be supported, psychosocial Support must be ensured for both teachers as well as learners, prioritizing the most vulnerable. And there is also the question of physical rehabilitation, especially for child amputees and prosthetics. Also for children, please remember, it's a long process continuously which has to be changed. They have to be mentored through as their bodies grow. This has to be changed. The funding needed must be robust, predictable, flexible, and multi-year. UNRWA's critical role must be preserved, and the legal bans and restrictions must be overturned. So, coordinated sustainable recovery needs strengthened regional partnerships and national systems, and I think bringing together UNRWA with the ministries of education, Palestinian organizations, UN partners, donors, and communities is essential. Otherwise, we will continue to witness the scholasticide, which is an intergenerational war. Thank you.
Thank you so much, Ms. Shahid, for sharing with us the current situation on the right to education in the OPT and also the numerous challenges faced by the children, students, and teachers, and also the importance of continued support for UNRWA in this current situation. So, the next contribution will come to us via video recorded message. Our next speaker is Mr. Srinivasan Muralidhar, Chair of the Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem and Israel. The Independent International Commission of Inquiry has also documented serious violations affecting civilians. Its recent works have addressed violence by Israeli settlers and Palestinian armed groups, and in a separate report, The Devastating Consequences of the Conflict for Palestinian Children. The Commission concluded that children have suffered extensive physical and psychological harm and profound disruption to almost every aspect of their lives. These findings remind us that education, development, and human rights cannot be separated from the conditions in which people live. Because of prior engagements, Mr. Muralithar could not attend today's event, but has kindly recorded a video message which will be played now.
Good morning, Chair, Excellencies, colleagues. Thank you for inviting me to this important event. I apologize for not being there in person. Regrettably, I have not received a visa despite my best efforts. and despite my fulfilling with all the requirements. As a result, I was unable to travel to New York to present the report of the Commission to the General Assembly earlier this week on Monday. I had to resort to an online presentation. The topic of this event is one of particular importance. Human dignity is not a new or emerging concern globally, but in the occupied Palestinian territory, it is a long-standing issue that has severely and adversely impacted the Palestinian people. We do not need to look too far back. In just the period since 7 October 2023, over 75,000 Palestinians across the occupied Palestinian territory have been killed, including at least 21,500 children and 11,000 women. In the West Bank alone, more than 1,080 Palestinians were killed, and 10,950 were injured by the Israeli forces between 7 October 2023 and 30 September 2026.
